routes.description: Establish that God is required to ground objective moral value and duty and to provide the ultimate significance and accountability that complete an objective moral framework.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if intrinsic value is grounded in God's nature, categorical duty in divine commands rather than convention, and the lasting significance and accountability of moral action in a theistic order.

motionBridge.description: Show that objective values, duties, human significance, and accountability jointly require God.

centralBridges.description: Ground intrinsic human worth and objective goodness in God's nature while explaining why naturalistic capacities or evolutionary origins are insufficient.
Ground categorical moral obligations in divine commands and distinguish genuine duties from social conditioning, agreement, or convention.
Explain why enduring moral significance and ultimate accountability require consequences beyond extinction and temporal human affairs.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain how divine accountability reconciles moral obligation with prudential reasons and supports responsible moral agency.
Distinguish fallible moral knowledge from objective truth and preserve transcultural criticism of conduct and institutions.

routes.description: Establish that stance-independent moral reasons, objective duties, human significance, and responsibility can be explained within secular moral realism without a divine ground or eternal consequences.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if secular accounts supply objective moral standards and categorical reasons, explain responsible agency and moral criticism, and show that finite harms, benefits, relationships, and actions retain real significance without cosmic permanence.

motionBridge.description: Show that secular moral realism can adequately ground every objective moral domain placed in dispute without requiring God.

centralBridges.description: Explain objective morality through desire-independent categorical reasons, substantive harm-and-help standards, or basic moral facts.
Explain moral requirements through decisive reasons or fair rational agreement without presupposing a personal lawgiver.
Ground genuine human significance in the objective importance of finite lives, harms, relationships, and actions rather than eternal cosmic effects.
Ground responsibility in rational agency and defend the authority of moral reasons even when morality conflicts with prudential self-interest.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain disagreement and historical moral error as compatible with objective truth and corrigible through reflective reasoning.
Demonstrate how secular principles yield determinate judgments about atrocities, innocent victims, and harms to sentient animals.

sections.title: Objective Value and Intrinsic Human Worth
sections.rationale: The motion requires an account of what makes value stance-independent and whether human worth is grounded by God, rational capacities, harm, or irreducible moral facts.

sections.title: Moral Duty, Categorical Reasons, and Lawgiving
sections.rationale: The principal grounding clash concerns whether genuine obligation needs divine command or can arise from objective reasons, rational agreement, and mutual moral authority.

sections.title: Rational Agency and Naturalistic Grounding
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether reflective capacities can explain moral responsibility and wrongness, or merely identify valuable features whose objective status still requires a deeper ground.

sections.title: Finite Life, Extinction, and Moral Significance
sections.rationale: The competing routes must establish whether actions and relationships need eternal consequences to matter objectively or possess genuine importance within finite human lives.

sections.title: Accountability, Salvation, and Prudential Conflict
sections.rationale: The accountability burden includes ultimate justice, the relation between morality and self-interest, and whether the proposed theistic mechanism consistently delivers deserved consequences.

sections.title: Moral Knowledge, Progress, and Practical Application
sections.rationale: Disagreement, historical error, atrocities, and treatment of animals test whether each foundation supports reliable moral criticism and substantive guidance without conflating access with truth.
